transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess what made me come in is that I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. 

I'm in a pipefitting apprenticeship right now, and... I don't know, I just feel like a total fake. Like I'm constantly letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices. It's usually over little mistakes, stuff that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from, but it just hangs over me and I feel like I'm failing them all.
How long have you been feeling this way — like you're letting people down and that you're a fake? Did this start recently, or has it been going on for a while?

I'd say it's been going on for a while. This whole depressed stretch has been with me for about nine months now. At first, I could kind of manage it, but... it just became a lot harder to hide once my classes and work at the apprenticeship started slipping.
During these nine months of feeling depressed, have there been any periods where you felt noticeably better or more like yourself, even if just for a few days or a week?

No, not really. It's just been this same heavy feeling the whole time. I don't think I've had any breaks from it where I felt like my normal self, even for a couple of days. It's just been a constant thing for the last nine months.
During these nine months, have there been any days where you felt completely fine or back to normal, even if just for a single day?
No, um... like I was saying, I really haven't had a single day like that. Not even for just one day. It's just been the exact same low feeling every day for the whole nine months.
During these nine months or even before that, have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, more talkative than usual, or like your mood was elevated or even euphoric?

Actually, before this whole depressed stretch started, yeah... there were a few weeks where I felt almost too good. It was like Miami was just mine. But at the same time, um... I was getting really irritated, too. Like, every little comment from a coworker who slowed me down on a job made me snap way harder than I normally would.
During those few weeks when you felt really good and energetic, did you notice that you needed less sleep than usual? Like, were you sleeping fewer hours but still feeling rested and energized?

Yeah, back then I was getting by on maybe three or four hours a night. I'd still show up completely wired for work and my classes. But now... now it's completely different. I either can't fall asleep at all, or I wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just feel like I never even rested.
When you were feeling really good and irritable before the depression started, how many days or weeks did that last? Was it just a few days, or did it go on for longer?

I'm not exactly sure how long it lasted, to be honest. I know it was more than just a few days, but I can't really put a specific number of weeks on it. It just felt like a stretch of time before everything crashed.
During those weeks when you felt really good and irritable, would you say it lasted at least a full week, or was it shorter than that?

I'm really not sure if it was a full seven days. Um... like I said, it was definitely more than just a couple of days, but I wasn't exactly keeping track of the calendar while it was happening. So I can't really give you a definite yes or no on if it made it to a full week.
When you were feeling really good and irritable, do you think that lasted at least 4 days in a row, or was it shorter than that?

I honestly couldn't tell you if it was exactly four days. Um... it was definitely a few days in a row, but like I said, I just wasn't paying close enough attention to the days of the week to give you a hard number. It might have been four, but I'm really just not sure.
Looking back, do you remember what day of the week it started and what day it ended? That might help us figure out if it was at least four days.

No, I really don't remember what day it started or ended. Um... my work schedule kind of makes the days of the week blur together for me anyway, so I wasn't paying attention to whether it was a Tuesday or a Friday. I wish I could give you a better timeline to help figure it out, but I honestly just don't know.
When you think back to that stretch of time when you felt really good and irritable, do you remember feeling that way for most of a week, or was it more like just a couple of days?

I know you're trying to get a specific timeframe, but... like I was saying before, I really just don't know. It felt like more than just a couple of days, but as far as whether it was most of a week, I honestly couldn't tell you. I just wasn't keeping track of it like that.
When you think back to that time when you felt really good and irritable, do you think that stretch lasted about as long as a long weekend, or was it shorter than that?

I'm sorry, I know you're trying to figure this out, but I really just can't say for sure. A long weekend... maybe? It's just a blur. I know it was a few days, but I can't confidently say if it was three days, four days, or what. I just don't have a clear memory of the exact timeline.

During that stretch when you felt really good and irritable, do you remember if you went to work or your apprenticeship classes during that time, and if so, how many days in a row did you show up feeling that way?

I'm not sure if I went to work or my classes while I was feeling like that. I mean, I usually go to work and my apprenticeship stuff when I'm supposed to, but I really can't remember if I was there during that specific time, or how many days in a row it might have been. Like I said, it's all just kind of a blur.

When you think back to that time when you felt really good and irritable, if you had to guess, do you think you felt that way for at least 3 or 4 days in a row, or do you think it was probably just 1 or 2 days?

If I really had to guess... I'd probably say it was at least three or four days in a row. It definitely felt longer than just a day or two. But again, I'm just guessing based on how it felt, I don't have a solid memory of the exact days.

You mentioned that stretch of feeling really good and irritable lasted at least 3 or 4 days. During those days, did you feel that way continuously — like from morning through the end of each day — or was it more on and off?

I honestly couldn't tell you. Um, since that whole time is such a blur, I don't really remember if it was every single minute from morning to night, or if it kind of came and went. I just know I felt that way generally over that stretch, but the actual day-to-day details... I just don't have them.

I know the exact timeline is fuzzy for you, but let me ask it this way: during that stretch when you felt really good and irritable, do you think it's more likely that you felt that way for at least 4 days in a row, or do you think it probably lasted less than 4 days?

I really don't know for sure. Like I said, it felt longer than a day or two, but whether it was exactly four days or less than four days... I just can't give you a straight answer on that. I'm really just guessing at this point.

Let me try asking this differently. During that stretch when you felt really good and irritable, did you miss any work or apprenticeship classes because you were feeling that way, or did you manage to keep going to your normal schedule?

I didn't really miss any days, no. I managed to keep going to my regular schedule for work and my classes. But... I wasn't exactly keeping up. My instructors and my foreman, they've had to chase me down a lot about unfinished sketches and just, you know, slower work in general. Honestly, I'm pretty scared that I'm close to damaging this apprenticeship and the certification I've worked really hard to get.

During that stretch when you felt really good and irritable, do you remember if you were working on any specific pipefitting projects or jobs? If so, do you recall how many days you were working on that same project while feeling that way?

Um, not really. I mean, we usually have a few different things going on at the site or in the shop, but I couldn't tell you exactly which project I was assigned to during that specific time. And since I can't even remember what job I was on, I definitely don't know how many days I spent on it while I was feeling like that. I just... I don't have those details.

When you think about that time you felt really good and irritable before the depression started, looking back now, do you think it's more accurate to say it was a brief mood swing that lasted just a day or two, or do you think it was a more substantial period that lasted several days?

I really couldn't tell you for sure. I mean, it definitely felt like more than just a day or two, but... I don't know if I'd call it a substantial period of several days either. It's just a blur, to be honest. I can't really pin down exactly how long it lasted.

I know you've said it's hard to remember the exact timeline, but let me ask you this: when you think back to that time before the depression started, do you feel more confident saying it lasted at least 4 days, or do you think it was probably shorter than that — like 2 or 3 days?

I honestly don't know. Like I said, it's all just a blur to me now. I can't say for sure if it was four days, or three days, or what. I just remember feeling that way before everything kind of crashed, but I really can't put a number on it.
